value_stream.name: Government Affairs, Public Policy & Industry Relations

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, Comms/PR (links to VS-14.3), Legal (links to VS-100), affected business units, Leadership
fields.Trigger: Emerging public issue; complements VS-14.3 crisis comms

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track emerging public issues affecting BuildRight's license to operate" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-issue of "Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms manage the issue" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "Govt Affairs Mgr capture outcomes and lessons, update issue" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: early identification and engagement; operational: coordinated messaging
Pain Points / Risks: - **Issue-escalation risk**: Failing to manage an issue before it becomes a crisis (links to VS-14.3); mitigated by early identification and engagement
- **Mixed-messaging risk**: Inconsistent BuildRight voice across stakeholders; mitigated by coordinated messaging
System Touchpoints: - Issue tracking; comms/PR (links to VS-14.3); risk register (links to VS-21.2); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms identify and track emerging public issues affecting BuildRight's license to operate (consumer/retail, labor, environmental, tax, supply chain, data); assess materiality and stakeholder sentiment

Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms manage the issue: position, messaging, stakeholder engagement (government W3356, industry W3358, community W3371, media W3373), and escalation to crisis comms when warranted (links to VS-14.3 W134/W1562)
Govt Affairs Mgr capture outcomes and lessons, update issue playbook, and feed insights to risk register (links to VS-21.2) and reputation monitoring (W3370)

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, Comms/Brand (links to VS-14.3), Strategy (links to VS-33), Leadership, ESG (links to VS-25.2)
fields.Trigger: Annual; strategy refresh; complements VS-14.3 brand

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-report of "Govt Affairs Mgr tailor the narrative to audiences" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor stakeholder perception and reputation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: authenticity and ESG substance; operational: monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Narrative-reality gap risk**: Positioning not matched by BuildRight practice (links to VS-25 ESG, VS-91 privacy); mitigated by authenticity and ESG substance
- **Perception-blindness risk**: Unknown negative sentiment; mitigated by monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Reputation/perception monitoring (links to VS-28.1); comms/brand (links to VS-14.3); ESG (links to VS-25.2)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms develop BuildRight's corporate positioning and stakeholder narrative for external-affairs audiences: purpose, economic contribution (jobs, tax, suppliers), sustainability (links to VS-25), community impact, and policy stance

Govt Affairs Mgr tailor the narrative to audiences (government, industry, community, media, investors) and align with brand/PR (links to VS-14.3) and ESG reporting (links to VS-25.2); train spokespeople
Govt Affairs Mgr monitor stakeholder perception and reputation (surveys, media sentiment, social), measure narrative resonance, and refine positioning

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, CSR (links to VS-14.3 W135), Store Ops (links to VS-07), ESG (links to VS-25.2), Comms (links to VS-14.3)
fields.Trigger: Community program; local stakeholder need; complements VS-76.3/W2673 (barangay)

workflows.name: Community Relations & Local Stakeholder Engagement (National Brand Level)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "footprint and brand" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with store-level LGU relations" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "Govt Affairs Mgr/CSR measure community impact and sentiment, integrate" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: alignment with VS-76; operational: CSR/ESG measurement
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fragmented-community-engagement risk**: National and store-level community efforts uncoordinated; mitigated by alignment with VS-76.3
- **Impact-blindness risk**: Community spend without measurable impact; mitigated by CSR/ESG measurement
System Touchpoints: - Community/CSR tracking (links to VS-14.3); ESG (links to VS-25.2); disaster response (links to VS-69); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/CSR develop the national community-relations strategy: programs (disaster response links to VS-69, community build/repair, livelihood/cooperative links to VS-94, education/skills), alignment to BuildRight's footprint and brand

Govt Affairs Mgr/Store Ops engage community stakeholders at the national brand level (local-government leagues, civic groups, NGOs, community leaders), coordinate with store-level LGU relations (links to VS-76.3 W2673/W2686) and disaster response (links to VS-69.3)
Govt Affairs Mgr/CSR measure community impact and sentiment, integrate with CSR reporting (links to VS-14.3 W135/W151) and ESG (links to VS-25.2), and report to leadership

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, Strategy (links to VS-33), affected SMEs, Innovation (links to VS-30), Legal (links to VS-100)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify and engage think-tanks, academic institutions, and policy-research…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track partnership value and influence on policy debate, manage…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: independence and transparency; operational: selection and tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Influence-perception risk**: Funded research seen as biased; mitigated by independence and transparency
- **Low-leverage risk**: Partnerships that don't inform policy or strategy; mitigated by selection and tracking
System Touchpoints: - Partnership tracking; records (links to VS-88); ethics (links to VS-86.3)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/Strategy identify and engage think-tanks, academic institutions, and policy-research bodies on retail/supply-chain/labor/sustainability policy; sponsor or commission research aligned to BuildRight's interests

Govt Affairs Mgr/SMEs contribute BuildRight data/expertise to research, participate in forums/roundtables, and use the evidence base to support advocacy (W3355) and thought leadership (links to VS-33.3)
Govt Affairs Mgr track partnership value and influence on policy debate, manage conflicts/independence (links to VS-86.3), and report outcomes (W3368)

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, Comms/PR (links to VS-14.3), Leadership/Speakers, Legal (links to VS-100)
fields.Trigger: Policy/industry news cycle; complements VS-14.3 PR

workflows.name: Media & Analyst Relations for Policy/Industry Topics

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify media/analyst opportunities on policy and industry topics" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms prepare spokespeople with policy/industry briefings, key" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor coverage and sentiment, measure reach/impact, and feed insights to…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: prepared messaging and follow-up; operational: briefings and discipline
Pain Points / Risks: - **Misquote risk**: Media misrepresents BuildRight position; mitigated by prepared messaging and follow-up
- **Off-message risk**: Spokesperson deviates from approved position; mitigated by briefings and discipline
System Touchpoints: - Media monitoring (links to VS-28.1); comms/PR (links to VS-14.3); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms identify media/analyst opportunities on policy and industry topics (op-eds, interviews, briefings, commentary) where BuildRight's voice adds value; coordinate with brand PR (links to VS-14.3 W143)
Govt Affairs Mgr/Comms prepare spokespeople with policy/industry briefings, key messages, and Q&A; conduct interviews/commentary within messaging discipline and legal review (links to VS-100)
Govt Affairs Mgr monitor coverage and sentiment, measure reach/impact, and feed insights to reputation monitoring (W3370) and issue management (W3369)

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, Risk (links to VS-21.2), Legal (links to VS-100), Strategy (links to VS-33), affected SMEs
fields.Trigger: Annual risk cycle; complements VS-21.2 ERM

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "enterprise risk register" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor risk indicators, update assessments as the environment changes, and…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-155 (ensure lawful political engagement & lobbying disclosure.)
- operational: horizon scanning (W3354) and scenario planning; operational: integration into ERM
Pain Points / Risks: - **Blind-spot risk**: Unforeseen political/regulatory shock; mitigated by horizon scanning (W3354) and scenario planning
- **Mitigation-gap risk**: Identified risks without mitigation owners; mitigated by integration into ERM
System Touchpoints: - Risk register (links to VS-21.2); BCP (links to VS-26); records (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/Risk assess political and regulatory risks: policy/legislative shifts (tax reform, retail regulation, labor, payments, data, customs/tariff links to VS-87), political instability, elections, geopolitical/supply-chain risk; estimate likelihood/impact

Govt Affairs Mgr/Risk develop mitigation strategies (advocacy W3355, compliance readiness links to VS-22.3, scenario/contingency planning links to VS-26 BCP, supply-chain resilience links to VS-02.3); integrate into the enterprise risk register (links to VS-21.2)
Govt Affairs Mgr monitor risk indicators, update assessments as the environment changes, and report political/regulatory risk to leadership and the board/audit committee (links to VS-21/VS-36)

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Procurement (links to VS-34), VP Legal & Compliance
fields.Trigger: Annual budget cycle (links to VS-33.1); monthly review

workflows.name: Government Affairs & Industry-Relations Budget, Spend & Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor spend vs budget monthly, manage exceptions and approvals" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-allocate of "reallocate to high-impact activities, and report spend and analytics to leadership" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: analytics and ROI tracking; operational: controls and disclosure
Pain Points / Risks: - **Spend-without-value risk**: External-affairs spend unmeasured; mitigated by analytics and ROI tracking
- **Ethics-breach risk**: Improper spend (contributions/hospitality) (links to VS-86.3); mitigated by controls and disclosure
System Touchpoints: - Budget/finance (links to VS-17.4); AP (links to VS-34/VS-17.1); ethics (links to VS-86.3); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/Finance build the external-affairs budget: memberships/dues (W3361), sponsorships (W3367), events (W3365), community/CSR (W3371), partnerships (W3372), advocacy, and travel; align to corporate budget (links to VS-33.1)
Govt Affairs Mgr monitor spend vs budget monthly, manage exceptions and approvals (links to VS-36), and ensure ethics/anti-bribery compliance on all external-affairs spend (links to VS-86.3/W3360)
Govt Affairs Mgr/Finance analyze spend effectiveness (value-per-dollar by program), reallocate to high-impact activities, and report spend and analytics to leadership

fields.Participants: Govt Affairs Mgr, VP Legal & Compliance, Leadership, BI (links to VS-28.1), Board (links to VS-36.1)
fields.Trigger: Annual planning; board reporting (links to VS-36.1)

workflows.name: External-Affairs Annual Plan, KPI & Board Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "footprint W3362/W3368, reputation W3370, risk indicators W3374" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report to the board" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-543 (ensure controlled execution — Public Affairs, Community Relations & Reputation (PA-104.3).)
- operational: KPI tracking and accountability; operational: quarterly reporting
Pain Points / Risks: - **Plan-execution-gap risk**: Ambitious plan without execution; mitigated by KPI tracking and accountability
- **Board-blindness risk**: Board unaware of external-affairs exposure; mitigated by quarterly reporting
System Touchpoints: - External-affairs analytics (links to VS-28.1); governance/board (links to VS-36); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr/VP Legal & Compliance develop the annual external-affairs plan: objectives (policy outcomes, industry influence, reputation, risk mitigation), initiatives, KPIs, and budget (W3375); align to corporate strategy (links to VS-33)
steps.r: Govt Affairs Mgr / VP Legal & Compliance

steps.activity: Govt Affairs Mgr track KPIs quarterly (policy engagements W3356, submissions W3357, coalition activity W3358, industry footprint W3362/W3368, reputation W3370, risk indicators W3374), and report to leadership

Govt Affairs Mgr/VP Legal & Compliance present the external-affairs report to the board (links to VS-36.1): policy landscape, key engagements and outcomes, industry standing, political/regulatory risks, and recommendations
steps.r: Govt Affairs Mgr / VP Legal & Compliance
